title: Valuation neighbourhoods and common finite Riemann--Zariski refinement
statement: Let $T$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, let $k(T)$ be its function field, and fix a separable closure $L$ of $k(T)$. An $L$-model is an integral scheme $T_i$ with a factorization $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T_i\to T$ taking the point to the generic point, with $T_i\to T$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. An $L$-quasi-model has instead $T_i\to T$ separated and of finite type. Thus the function fields of these models are finite separable extensions of $k(T)$. Define $RZ_L(T)$ as the space of compatible families of points in all $L$-models, with the coarsest topology making all projections continuous. This space is quasi-compact, and its points are precisely centred valuation rings $V$ of $L$ together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}V\to T$ agreeing with the generic map. Each such $V$ has finite height. An $L$-quasi-model $U$ gives an open injection $RZ_L(U)\hookrightarrow RZ_L(T)$. These opens cover $RZ_L(T)$ whenever the quasi-models give a neighbourhood for every valuation point. For finitely many $L$-quasi-models $U_i$, there is an $L$-model $T'\to T$ and open subschemes $W_i\subset T'$ with proper dominant $T$-morphisms $W_i\to U_i$ (that is, the composite $W_i\to U_i\to T$ equals $W_i\subset T'\to T$) having finite separable generic field extensions, compatible with the maps from $\operatorname{Spec}L$. If the opens $RZ_L(U_i)$ cover $RZ_L(T)$, the $W_i$ cover $T'$. Finite type for scheme morphisms has the meaning of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
